senses.sense_definition: A dishonest person who deceives or cheats others, often for illegal gain.

examples.text: The elderly woman was conned out of her life savings by a clever <w>trickster</w>.
Police warned citizens not to give bank details to an online <w>trickster</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A person who plays pranks, jokes, or practical tricks on other people.

examples.text: The school <w>trickster</w> loved hiding plastic spiders inside the teacher's desk drawer.
He was known among his friends as a mischievous <w>trickster</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A recurring character in folklore, mythology, or literature who uses wit and deceit to defy norms and challenge authority.

examples.text: In Norse mythology, Loki is famous as a cunning <w>trickster</w> god.
Many indigenous tales feature the coyote as a clever <w>trickster</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A playfully impish or mischievous individual.

examples.text: The little boy smiled like an impish <w>trickster</w> after hiding his sister's favorite toy.
She was a charming <w>trickster</w> who always knew how to make people laugh.

senses.sense_definition: A performer who executes magic tricks, illusions, or impressive physical stunts.

examples.text: The street <w>trickster</w> gathered a huge crowd with his sleight-of-hand card routines.
Audiences were astonished by the skilled <w>trickster</w> juggling knives on stage.

senses.sense_definition: To engage in trickery or behave like a trickster; to play tricks.

examples.text: He spent the whole afternoon trying to <w>trickster</w> his way out of doing chores.
The dishonest merchant tried to <w>trickster</w> unsuspecting shoppers at the market.
